CVE-2024-53150.title: ALSA: usb-audio: Fix out of bounds reads when finding clock sources
CVE-2024-53150.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

ALSA: usb-audio: Fix out of bounds reads when finding clock sources

The current USB-audio driver code doesn't check bLength of each
descriptor at traversing for clock descriptors. That is, when a
device provides a bogus descriptor with a shorter bLength, the driver
might hit out-of-bounds reads.

For addressing it, this patch adds sanity checks to the validator
functions for the clock descriptor traversal. When the descriptor
length is shorter than expected, it's skipped in the loop.

For the clock source and clock multiplier descriptors, we can just
check bLength against the sizeof() of each descriptor type.
OTOH, the clock selector descriptor of UAC2 and UAC3 has an array
of bNrInPins elements and two more fields at its tail, hence those
have to be checked in addition to the sizeof() check.

kev.name: Linux Kernel Out-of-Bounds Read Vulnerability
kev.required_action: Apply mitigations per vendor instructions, follow applicable BOD 22-01 guidance for cloud services, or discontinue use of the product if mitigations are unavailable.
kev.notes: This vulnerability affects a common open-source component, third-party library, or a protocol used by different products. For more information, please see: https://lore.kernel.org/linux-cve-announce/2024122427-CVE-2024-53150-3a7d@gregkh/ ; https://source.android.com/docs/security/bulletin/2025-04-01 ; https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2024-53150

CVE-2026-129538.title: PHP-CGI out-of-bounds read and write during PATH_INFO correction
CVE-2026-129538.description:
PHP-CGI out-of-bounds read and write during PATH_INFO correction.

The PHP CGI binary (php-cgi), in CGI and FastCGI mode with cgi.fix_pathinfo enabled (the default), can perform an out-of-bounds read and write when the path removed from SCRIPT_FILENAME or PATH_TRANSLATED is longer than the supplied PATH_INFO, or when PATH_INFO is empty. This requires a web server mapping that passes such inconsistent values, or a FastCGI listener reachable by untrusted clients. An unauthenticated remote attacker can crash the process, may obtain process memory if the application exposes PATH_INFO or PATH_TRANSLATED, and may corrupt memory. PHP-FPM and the Apache module are not affected.

This issue affects PHP versions before 8.2.36, 8.3.* before 8.3.37, 8.4.* before 8.4.28 and 8.5.* before 8.5.13.

CVE-2026-49869.title: Kestra: Unauthenticated Remote Code Execution via Authentication Bypass in `AuthenticationFilter`
CVE-2026-49869.description: Kestra is an open-source, event-driven orchestration platform. Prior to 1.0.45 and 1.3.21, AuthenticationFilter in Kestra OSS uses request.getPath().endsWith("/configs") to whitelist the public configuration endpoint from Basic Auth. Because the check is a suffix match rather than an exact path match, any API path whose last segment is configs bypasses authentication entirely. An unauthenticated remote attacker can exploit this to create and execute arbitrary workflows without credentials. Because Kestra ships with script execution plugins (plugin-script-shell, plugin-script-python, etc.) enabled by default, this directly results in unauthenticated Remote Code Execution as root inside the Kestra worker container. This vulnerability is fixed in 1.0.45 and 1.3.21.

CVE-2026-63393.title: OpenSearch SQL plugin: Unsafe cursor deserialization permits server code execution
CVE-2026-63393.description: OpenSearch SQL supports querying OpenSearch data using SQL and Piped Processing Language. In the 2.x line from 2.8.0.0 until 2.19.6.0, and the 3.x line prior to 3.7.0.0, a remote authenticated user with basic read/search permissions can provide a crafted `cursor` parameter to the `plugins/sql` endpoint and trigger unsafe deserialization of untrusted data, resulting in arbitrary code execution on the server. This issue is fixed in repository releases 2.19.6.0 and 3.7.0.0.

CVE-2026-65971.title: Livewire PowerGrid: SQL Injection through the public `sortDirection` Livewire property in the `naturalSort` order-by path
CVE-2026-65971.description: Livewire PowerGrid creates data tables based on Laravel Livewire library. From version 6.0.0 to before version 6.10.4, the public Livewire property sortDirection is interpolated verbatim into a raw SQL ORDER BY clause and is not restricted to asc/desc, allowing arbitrary SQL injection through POST /livewire/update. This issue has been patched in version 6.10.4.

CVE-2026-93585.title: Authenticated Remote Code Execution in EV Reach Client Agent
CVE-2026-93585.description:
An improper authorization vulnerability in the EasyVistas EV Reach Client Agent allows authenticated users with low privileges to execute arbitrary commands on a remote Windows endpoint with LocalSystem privileges. The affected agent service does not sufficiently enforce authorization restrictions for certain privileged remote management operations. Under specific conditions, the agent fails to apply the intended user impersonation mechanism and executes user-supplied commands within the security context of the agent service, which runs as NT AUTHORITY\SYSTEM.

As a result, an authenticated attacker may bypass the intended privilege restrictions and execute arbitrary commands with the highest user-mode privileges on an affected Windows system. CVE-2026-99378.title: pnfs/blocklayout: Complete a device upcall when the pipe is closed
CVE-2026-99378.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

pnfs/blocklayout: Complete a device upcall when the pipe is closed

Once blkmapd has read a whole upcall, rpc_pipe_read() unlinks the
message from every pipe list, so the purges in rpc_pipe_release()
and rpc_close_pipes() no longer reach it. bl_upcall_ops supplies no
.release_pipe callback, and bl_pipe_destroy_msg() returns without
completing the upcall because a downcall is expected to follow. A
daemon that exits between the read and the write therefore strands
its waiter: bl_resolve_deviceid() sleeps in wait_for_completion()
and never returns, and it holds nn->bl_mutex across that wait, so
every later device resolution in the net namespace blocks behind
it.

Add a .release_pipe that completes an upcall blkmapd has consumed
and left unanswered. Completing an upcall retires it, so a message
the framework has already purged is no longer in flight and is not
completed a second time here.
